messages:
maria_ng: Quick recap from todays mini-canary: speculative decode + q4-int8 emulation on titan-13b. notable: median latency improvement, but a small cluster of failures in constrained edit tasks. posting early notes so we don't lose context.
alex_ryan: thanks. short summary numbers?
maria_ng: pulled a tiny table from the harness:
```csv
variant,median_ms,p95_ms,inst-follow-fail_pct,rewrite-bleu_drop
baseline,125,315,0.7,0.0
speculative+q4,98,238,2.1,5.4
speculative-only,105,250,0.9,0.6
q4-only,120,302,1.4,1.8
```
samuel: BLEU drop concentrated on the "rewrite" microbench. low-diversity targets where exact token choice matters.
jin-ml: i inspected diffs: most regressions are single-token substitutions at commit boundary, often determiners or punctuation. points to commit timing + logit perturbation.
alex_ryan: did any shards show different KV-cache behavior? curious about eviction-coupled regressions.
maria_ng: 2 shards rolled back; their evict rate was 22% higher during load spike. those shards also had slightly older prefetched KV entries (by age distribution).
samuel: that suggests speculative prefetch may read stale context pieces if eviction cycles are aggressive. if commit uses stale KV, tokens could be wrong.
jin-ml: config used: `spec.enabled=true`, `spec.threshold=0.65`, `spec.max_lookahead=4`, `quant.mode=q4_emul`, `kv.policy=adaptive_lfu`.
alex_ryan: interesting. threshold 0.65 is relatively aggressive. can we try conservative thresholds in a quick run?
maria_ng: plan: run 3 short holdouts (4h each) with thresholds 0.5, 0.7, 0.85 and collect token-stability metrics. also add per-token "commit_conf_delta" (logit diff between top1 and runner-up at commit).
samuel: add a token-stability score: frequency of top-1 flip between quantized kernel and fp32 reference per token. that'll show where quantization amplifies uncertainty.
jin-ml: will instrument that. also proposing a small adversarial rewrite set (200 examples) where we vary punctuation and casing to stress boundary commits.
alex_ryan: for eval, use both BLEU and a binary exact-match where applicable. BLEU can mask single-token failures in short rewrites.
maria_ng: good call. i'll update harness to output both. also we'll keep RNG seed constant across variants to isolate quant/spec interactions.
samuel: one more hypothesis: sampling/postprocessing differences between kernels. speculative might commit before post-normalization steps (e.g., canonicalization for spacing). ensure commit point compares post-processed tokens.
injunk: sorry accidental typo
jin-ml: good point, samuel. will ensure commit trace logs capture tokens pre/post normalization.
maria_ng: ops-bot, can you schedule the three runs on 12 shards each? want them staggered to avoid noisy interference.
ops-bot: Job `spec-q4-threshold-scan-180600` created by maria_ng. shards: 12 each. ETA start in 2h.

alex_ryan: also create a small "q8-emulation" quick test as an intermediate quantization level; if errors drop substantially it indicates quant noise floor.
maria_ng: adding that to the job plan.
samuel: remember privacy: logs should contain token ids and diffs only, no free-text payloads.
maria_ng: agreed, scrubbed. i'll open a PR with harness changes and test vectors, tag @jin-ml and @alex_ryan for review.
jin-ml: i'll review the exporter today.
maria_ng: thanks all. we'll reconvene after run completions and post sanitized summaries here.
